NB. I don't really know much C# and I hope I didn't make mathematical errors.

I dug a little around Voat's source code and found the code for front page. There's a long query that ends .OrderByDescending(s => s.Rank). So it orders the posts by descending rank. The rank is calculated in Utils/Ranking.cs:

var newRank = (Math.Pow((score - 1), 0.8)) / (Math.Pow((submissionAge + 2), 1.8)) * penalty;

Written in a less programmer-y way that becomes newRank = (score - 1)^0.8/ ((submissionAge+2)^1.8)*penalty. It does this:

  • take the score of the post
  • subtract one from that
  • raise the result to power 0.8. Call the result x.
  • take the submission's age in hours
  • add two hours to the age
  • raise the result to power 1.8. Call this result y
  • calculate x/y
  • multiply the result of this division by "penalty", which is defined to be 1 in the source, it doesn't do anything. Hm, if the precedence in C# is the expected, this multiplication happens last and isn't taken into "y". But as I said, it doesn't do anything since the penalty is 1.

If the score happens to be zero or negative, the raising to power of 0.8 doesn't give an answer, so the code gives rank of zero instead.

I made an example calculation with 25 items. They don't need titles but I used alphabet :p

Is it true you should replace all your tires at one time? Is so why.
Its perfectly acceptable to replace them two at a time as long as they are all properly rotated.

I'll start a new post if this doesn't get answered in here, but it's kind of related. I was told that I should replace all tires at once because I have a four wheel drive vehicle. Does that make a difference?

Edit: When I did have to replace my tires, I replaced 2 at the same time, just not all 4 like the guy at the tire shop suggested.

Check the sidewalls to see if they're exactly the same size (if you're not familiar with tire sizing, it'll probably look something like 215/60R16 - numbers will differ but the format's the same on most modern tires.)

If they're even one size off, you're probably going to be looking at a very expensive repair bill in the not-too-distant future. Even if they're the same, the difference in wear or the slight difference in composition from one tire brand/model to another could be enough to fry your transfer case/central diff over the course of tens of thousands of miles - a very costly repair.

If your tires were taken care of properly they should all wear at the same pace, so it would be obvious to replace them all at the same time. Technically you could replace them 2 at a time, but if they aren't all wearing at the same time you're doing something wrong. And they would just look weird not matching.
